images.obtainFrom: Download the vJunos-router qcow2 from Juniper's software downloads and package it as a containerlab vrnetlab image, or set VJUNOS_ROUTER_IMAGE to the tag you already have.

checks.description: The route reflector p1 has an established VPN-capable BGP session to pe1.
The route reflector p1 has an established VPN-capable BGP session to pe2.
p1 has an operational LDP session to the pe1 loopback.
p1 has an operational LDP session to the pe2 loopback.

checks.command: show route table CUST-A.inet.0 198.51.100.1/32 exact | display json
checks.description: The remote customer site loopback is present in the CUST-A table on pe1, learned by BGP.
checks.hint: A VPN route only lands in a local table when the local instance imports the route target the far end attached to it. Check both ends of that agreement, not just the session state.

checks.command: show route table SITE1.inet.0 198.51.100.1/32 exact | display json
checks.description: The customer edge learns the remote site loopback, by BGP, in the site it reaches through pe1.
checks.hint: The customer only hears what pe1 tells it. If pe1 holds the remote route but the customer does not, look at the session between them, and at what the customer does with a route whose path already contains its own autonomous system.

checks.command: ping routing-instance SITE1 198.51.100.1 count 3 | display json
checks.description: The customer site reached through pe1 can reach the remote site loopback across the provider.
checks.hint: A route in one direction is half a conversation. The reply needs a route back to the address the request was sent from, so check what the far site has learned as well.

checks.description: pe1 reports the circuit to the remote provider edge as up, carrying virtual circuit 200.
checks.hint: A circuit needs three things to agree: the access port must be presented as a circuit rather than a routed interface, both ends must use the same circuit identifier, and the remote end must be reachable by the transport label path the core already provides.

checks.description: The remote provider edge agrees: it reports its side of virtual circuit 200 toward pe1 as up.
checks.hint: A circuit is signalled by both ends. When the far end is still waiting, it says so in its own connection status, and the legend in that output names what it is waiting for.
